what: lattice-claims, ported whole: the package (grader, taskset, forgeries, policies, CLI), its tests, the eval scripts, and the records — 135 rollouts, 45 wiring rollouts, the four refutation facts, the 24 overflow-cliff instances, and the page data.
history: The records came first (the same afternoon; the eval PROVENANCE this file replaces pinned results.json and refutations.json). The package snapshot here was one session behind the grader that graded those records — taskset.py and forgeries.py stale, policies.py and __main__.py absent — which frontier's PORT-TO-CERT-MACHINE.md (session 17) named. This is the update.
why: The pinned rollouts are the RE-GRADED record; a grader that is not the one that graded them is a claim about a different set. eval/regrade.py measures exactly that against the stored raws and must report 0 rows moved — instruments/wiring/battery.py runs it every build.
rule: Copied byte-for-byte and pinned by sha256; frontier-apps has no git, so the hash is the only pin. The source tree is read-only. Nothing here is a lift from sin-mfg. Model calls (eval/run_models.py) are never made by a battery; the record is what was run there.

files.patch: was empty (0 bytes). Now the package docstring, the stdlib re-exports, the version read from installed metadata rather than written twice, and the LAZY resolver for `load_environment` — the Hub's entry point, which the first environment of this family once shipped without exporting.
a three-line `cli()` added so the console script declared in pyproject and the `python -m lattice_claims` form share one body.
imports the parser from the package rather than from run_models, so the regrade exercises the one definition directly instead of transitively.

its private `parse()` replaced by `from lattice_claims.api import parse_reply as parse`. The function moved into the package unchanged so the framework adapter and this runner cannot read a reply by two rules; the battery re-grades all 135 stored raws with the package's copy every build and no row may move.

four sections rewritten on the port because the Hub renders this file as the environment's front page and all four were false here: there was NO install section at all; Layout said 18 tests (there are 27) and omitted api.py and adapters_v0.py; Reproduce invoked a builder that does not exist in this repository; and Page pointed at site/lattice-claims built by tools/build-lattice-env.js, when it is /instruments/lattice-claims built by playground/build.js. Two sections added: the verified binding and the live run.

rewritten from a twelve-line stub to the publishable shape: readme, license, authors, the Hub tags, `dependencies = ["verifiers>=0.2.0"]`, urls, the console script, hatchling, and a requires-python floor of 3.11 — the floor of the WHEEL (verifiers needs it), not of the grader, which is stdlib and runs on 3.9 in this repository's battery.

publishingLayer.what: The publishing layer added 2026-09-10, following the pattern blind-spot proved out: api.py (framework-free surface), adapters_v0.py (load_environment), lazy exports, the publishable pyproject, and the two binding tests.
publishingLayer.adapter: Written against a LIVE verifiers 0.3.1 and then run against live models. The three defects a doc-written binding produced in break-the-grader are each designed out and each has a test; all nine binding + framework-free tests passed on the first run, because the four framework facts were already known from the sibling port.
publishingLayer.cleanInstall: pip install of the built wheel into a fresh 3.12 venv, loaded from /tmp with no source tree: SingleTurnEnv, 6 train / 6 eval across all three rungs, no answer column, no task column, disjoint seeds. And the thesis reaches the framework layer: a right verdict from a reference the task did not state scores reward 1.0 and well_formed 0.0.

liveRun.what: 72 rollouts through verifiers against two live models, 0 disagreements between the framework's reward and this package's own scoring of the same completions.
liveRun.finding: HAIKU 4.5 SCORED 4 of 12 CERTIFIED ON THE `declared` RUNG AND 0 OF 12 WELL FORMED — every verdict it got right came from a reference it never properly declared. That is the environment's whole thesis appearing as a measurement: exactness without naming what you were exact about.
liveRun.opusNotRun: claude-opus-5 was not run: the account's credit balance ran out. The 400 arrives before any generation, so nothing was billed for it, and the 24-rollout record it produced was DELETED rather than kept — those were billing failures, not model results.
